The passage describes the Treaty of Tordesillas, which established a line of demarcation dividing newly discovered lands between Spain and Portugal in the Atlantic Ocean. This treaty was made possible by advances in navigation that allowed sailors to determine their position at sea with greater accuracy, particularly in establishing longitude (though imperfectly at the time). The compass was essential for maritime navigation by enabling sailors to maintain direction across open ocean, which directly facilitated the voyages of discovery that led to the territorial disputes resolved by this treaty.
